text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Embattled opposition leader Michael Kijana Wamalwa now faces another scandal over the source of 7.5 million shillings spent in the January FORD-Kenya national elections.
- Four senior policemen, among them a deputy commissioner, are sent on compulsory leave over the December 18 killing of two Kenyatta University students.
- The Ministry of Education says the secondary school entry deadline is end of February.

- Kenya's parliamentary watchdog Public Accounts Committee formally disown their chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa over controversial letters written to business tycoon Ketan Somaia which cleared him of allegations that he failed to supply equipment to the government when he had already been paid.
- South Africa sets up a committee to probe Somaia's track record after his controversial Mpumalanga National Park deal.
- The tiny opposition Social Democratic Party of Kenya has threatened to sue the Kenya Times daily newspaper for claiming the party intended to introduce guerrilla warfare in Kenya.
- FORD-Kenya's first vice-chairman James Orengo is forced to swallow his challenge to chairman Wamalwa and offers his unreserved apology to the party for criticising his boss.
- The government is urged to lift the ban on controversial anti-AIDS drug Pearl Omega researched by Professor Arthur Obel.
- Nairobi City Council Mayor Dick Waweru pledges to set aside jobs for women as a step toward curbing social problems like street children.
